faq: Where does my help content need to live?
On web pages we can read, such as a Shopify page, WordPress, Zendesk, Help Scout or Notion site. If it is in documents only, we turn them into pages or a searchable sheet first.
Does it replace my current search?
It sits beside or on top of it. We can keep your existing search as a fallback so that nothing breaks if the new one cannot find a match.
It only returns text from your own articles and always links to the source. If an article is out of date, the answer will be too, so we flag stale pages we notice.
How does it stay current when I add articles?
New articles are picked up on a schedule we set, usually daily. We explain how to trigger an update by hand when you publish something urgent.

desc:
AI help center search for customers lets people type a plain question and land on the right article. Ecom Swift LLC adds meaning-based search to your existing help pages, so customers find answers faster and your team answers fewer repeat questions.

## What is AI help center search?

AI help center search is a search box that matches the meaning of a question, not only the exact words. A customer who types "where is my parcel" reaches your delivery article even if the article says "shipping and tracking". The search reads your published help pages, shows the best matches and can add a short answer above the links.

## Why keyword-only search leaves customers stranded

Standard help center search looks for the same words the customer typed. People rarely use your vocabulary. They write "money back" when your page says "refund", or "cancel" when you wrote "terminate subscription". The search returns nothing, the customer assumes you have no answer and opens a support ticket.

Every failed search is a missed chance to help. It also hides information from you, because a search that returns nothing leaves no trace of what the customer wanted.

## How better search reduces tickets and frustration

When customers find the answer themselves, the question never reaches your inbox. Your team spends less time on routine questions and more on cases that need a person. Customers also prefer a fast answer to waiting for a reply, particularly outside business hours.

The second benefit is learning. A list of searches that found nothing shows exactly where your help content has gaps. You can write the missing article once and answer that question for every future customer.

## What a strong help search includes

- Search that understands everyday phrasing, misspellings and short questions.
- Results ranked by relevance, with the best three articles shown first.
- A short answer drawn from your own article text, with a link to the full page.
- A clear message when no good answer exists, with your contact options beside it.
- Synonyms for your product names, nicknames and common abbreviations.
- Styling that matches your site fonts and colors.
- A record of searches that returned nothing useful.
- A simple routine for adding new articles to the search.
- Placement on the help page, and optionally on product pages.

## How we build it

We review your help content and check where it lives, whether in a Shopify page set, a Zendesk or similar help center, a Notion site or plain pages on your own website. We connect the search to those pages, tune how results are ranked and test it with real customer questions you supply.

The Basic package covers a smaller set of articles on one help page. The Standard package adds short answers above the links, a list of failed searches, matching site styling and a larger test. The Premium package adds synonyms for your product names, suggestions for articles to write next, search on your product pages and an update guide. The answers only ever draw on your published articles, so the search does not invent policies.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Keep one article per question, with a plain title.
- Review the failed search list every month.
- Write titles the way customers speak.
- Retest after you change shipping or return rules.

**Avoid:**
- Burying key answers inside long pages.
- Leaving outdated articles live next to new ones.
- Treating the search as a replacement for contact options.
- Using internal jargon in article titles.
- Adding hundreds of thin articles that repeat each other.

## Who this is for

An online store whose delivery and returns pages exist but customers still email the same questions. A software or service business with a growing help center that nobody can navigate. A small team that wants to see what customers cannot find before deciding what to write next.

## What we need from you

Send the address of your help pages or an export of the articles. Give us access as a collaborator, staff or developer user where your platform supports it, never a password. Tell us your product names and the questions customers ask most, and we will build the first test set from them.
